facts.fact: As of 2026-10-16, FRED ICSA has no observation for the week ending 2026-10-17; the latest observation is the week ending 2026-10-10, and the next release date shown is 2026-10-22.
On 2026-10-15, the Department of Labor's first published seasonally adjusted initial claims for the week ending 2026-10-10 were 199,000.

That 199,000 figure is not above 199,000; the four prior revised weekly levels on the 2026-10-15 FRED vintage were 198,000 (2026-09-12), 198,000 (2026-09-19), 199,000 (2026-09-26), and 198,000 (2026-10-03).

The first published level for the week ending 2026-10-03 was 197,000; the 2026-10-15 release revised it to 198,000.
Resolution of the 2026-10-17 week uses only the first published ICSA value.

The FRED release calendar lists the Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report for Thursday, 2026-10-22, at 7:30 a.m., and that Thursday is not among ETA's listed holiday exceptions (which move the release off Thursday).

ETA states the weekly claims news release is published each Thursday at 8:30 a.m.
EST except when Thursday is a federal holiday.
Unadjusted initial claims for the week ending 2026-10-10 were 190,626, up 11.4 percent, while seasonal factors had expected an 11.0 percent increase.
On the revised FRED vintage retrieved 2026-10-16, 32 of 41 weekly ICSA observations from the week ending 2026-01-03 through 2026-10-10 were strictly above 199,000, and 0 of the latest 4 weeks were.

uncertainties: The first published ICSA value for the week ending 2026-10-17 does not exist yet and is scheduled for release on 2026-10-22.
A print of exactly 199,000 would not be above 199,000; recent revised weeks have sat at 198,000 or 199,000.
Seasonal factors for the week ending 2026-10-17 are not in the 2026-10-15 release, and the prior week's unadjusted change already differed from the factor the Department had expected.
The prior week's first print was revised by 1,000 claims, so the level that will be revised later can differ from the first print that decides this question.
No advance state-by-state initial-claims changes for the week ending 2026-10-17 were in the 2026-10-15 release.

quotes: In the week ending October 10, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial claims was 199,000, an increase of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level.
The previous week's level was revised up by 1,000 from 197,000 to 198,000.
The advance number of actual initial claims under state programs, unadjusted, totaled 190,626 in the week ending October 10, an increase of 19,456 (or 11.4 percent) from the previous week.
